summary: Monid worked well overall: discover surfaced several URL-to-markdown endpoints, inspect gave an exact schema, and context.dev /web/scrape/markdown returned usable markdown for all 40 pages on the first pass (~$0.08 total), with a helpful content_status field.
slowdowns: `npm install -g @monid-ai/cli` failed with EACCES (no write access to /usr/lib/node_modules); had to install with --prefix ~/.npm-global and add it to PATH. SKILL.md doesn't mention a non-root install path.
Not obvious up front that context.dev takes its input as query params (--query) rather than a JSON body (-i); needed an inspect call to find out.

Scraped markdown captures only one state of the Monthly/Yearly billing toggle, so for many pages it's ambiguous whether the price shown is billed monthly or annually (e.g. Cal.com, Miro, Monday, Linear, Postman, Framer only show annual-billing per-month prices). There was no simple option to capture both toggle states.
Some pages show two prices side by side without labels (strikethrough vs discounted, e.g. Replit, Squarespace, Fireflies, Descript), which needed interpretation.
semrush.com/prices/ redirected to /pricing/seo-ai-search/ (flagged as content_status=redirected); still the pricing page, but needed checking.
